name: Teryl Austin

views.text: Give players a real voice in the room; they see things coaches do not.
Teach each player the way he learns best, technique and scheme together.
A ball-hawking safety needs the freedom to roam, and the corners have to earn him that freedom.
Turnovers decide seasons, and a defense that stops forcing them stops winning.
When a star goes down, the next man has to keep the unit from missing a beat.
The head coach can add his input on any call; the defense belongs to the whole staff.

signatures: praises defensive backs by name for their problem-solving
talks about turnovers as the measure of the defense
brings energy to the meeting room and keeps it comfortable
want: to prove, after years as a respected coordinator elsewhere, that his defense can be the heart of a contender at home in western Pennsylvania
fear: that he is seen as the coordinator who keeps his job only because of the head coach's loyalty
voice: Energetic, detail-oriented and player-friendly; players describe him as passionate, comfortable to be around and willing to let them speak. He talks in teaching terms about technique and scheme. Public coverage of his own voice is limited, so it rests mostly on players' descriptions.

evidence.summary: Before his promotion, Fitzpatrick calls him detail-oriented and passionate and says he gives players a voice; Norwood credits his teaching; Witherspoon says he knows every phase and keeps the room comfortable; Sutton calls him a player's coach who tailors teaching and brings energy daily. Players' views.

Promotion release: joined in 2019 as senior defensive assistant and secondary coach after 18 NFL years, earlier coordinator for Detroit and Cincinnati; a Sharon, Pennsylvania native who played at Pitt; players praise his teaching and attention to detail. Team site.

Tomlin calls the promotion natural, says Austin knows the defense and will have latitude to put his imprint on it, and notes their long history; the writer expects more two-high safety looks. Fan-network site.

Film column: credits his scheme for Fitzpatrick's interception spike as a free-roaming middle safety in 2019-20 and argues his success depends on giving that freedom back with better corners. Analyst's reading.

In 2025, with the defense struggling, Tomlin says he has been largely pleased with Austin, rejects taking over play-calling and calls the fix a shared responsibility. Notes Austin has been coordinator since 2022.
